#!/usr/bin/env bash
#SBATCH --partition=cpu
#SBATCH --job-name=snakemake
#SBATCH --ntasks=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=1
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --mem=2G
#SBATCH --time=3-00:00:00
#SBATCH --output=%j.txt
#SBATCH --error=%j.err

source ~/.bashrc
conda activate snakemake


##### uncomment as you wish ######

# single sample cluster
#snakemake Mutect2/temp/multi/RFH001_norm.vcf.gz --latency-wait 100 --rerun-incomplete -p \
#--cluster "sbatch --ntasks 1 --cpus-per-task {threads} --partition cpu --job-name {rule} --time 5:00:00 -e logs/{rule}/{params.err} -o logs/{rule}/{params.out} --mem {resources.mem_mb} --parsable" \
#--jobs 10 --keep-going --use-envmodules --cluster-status ./status-sacct.sh

#single sample local
#snakemake Mutect2/multi/RFH001.vcf.gz --latency-wait 100 --rerun-incomplete -p --use-envmodules -c1

#all cluster
snakemake -n --latency-wait 100 --rerun-incomplete -p \
--cluster "sbatch --ntasks 1 --cpus-per-task {threads} --partition cpu --job-name {rule} --time 5:00:00 -e logs/{rule}/{params.err} -o logs/{rule}/{params.out} --mem {resources.mem_mb} --parsable" \
--jobs 500 --keep-going --use-envmodules --cluster-status ./status-sacct.sh

#singe samle dryrun
#snakemake Mutect2/multi/RFH001.vcf.gz --rerun-incomplete -p --use-envmodules --dry-run

#all dryrun
#snakemake --rerun-incomplete -p --use-envmodules --dry-run

issues: The active `snakemake` command includes the `-n` (or `--dry-run`) flag. This means the workflow will not execute any jobs but will only print the commands that would be run. This is likely not the intended behavior for an actual production run.

The `--jobs 500` argument instructs Snakemake to attempt submitting up to 500 jobs to the scheduler simultaneously. This may overwhelm the scheduler or exceed user/system-wide job submission limits. Consider a more conservative number.

The main job requests minimal resources (`--cpus-per-task=1`, `--mem=2G`), which is generally correct for a Snakemake master process that only submits other jobs. Ensure that the resources requested within the `--cluster` submission string (e.g., `{threads}`, `{resources.mem_mb}`) are appropriately defined in the Snakefile for each rule.
There is a minor typo in a commented-out line: '#singe samle dryrun' should be '#single sample dryrun'.
